concept.title: Acintyabhedābheda
concept.description: The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava doctrine of acintyabhedābheda (inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference), associated with Jīva Gosvāmī, stating that the relationship between Kṛṣṇa and his potencies is beyond logical categorization; its epistemological and theological implications are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava doctrine of acintyabhedābheda (inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference), associated with Jīva Gosvāmī, stating that the relationship between Kṛṣṇa and his potencies is beyond logical categorization; its epistemological and theological implications are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Advaita Adhyāsa
concept.description: In Advaita Vedānta, adhyāsa (superimposition) is the erroneous attribution of the qualities of the non-self (anatman) to the self (ātman); its definition, types (svarūpa and samsarga), and role in bondage are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
In Advaita Vedānta, adhyāsa (superimposition) is the erroneous attribution of the qualities of the non-self (anatman) to the self (ātman); its definition, types (svarūpa and samsarga), and role in bondage are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Advaita Ajāti-vāda
concept.description: The Advaita doctrine of ajāti-vāda (non-origination), associated with Gauḍapāda, asserting that the world of birth and death never truly originates and that Brahman alone is real; its arguments and relation to Māṇḍūkya Kārikā are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Advaita doctrine of ajāti-vāda (non-origination), associated with Gauḍapāda, asserting that the world of birth and death never truly originates and that Brahman alone is real; its arguments and relation to Māṇḍūkya Kārikā are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Advaita Avidyā
concept.description: In Advaita Vedānta, avidyā (nescience) is the beginningless ignorance that veils Brahman and projects the world of multiplicity; its nature as neither real nor unreal (anirvacanīya), its locus, and its removal through brahma-jñāna are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
In Advaita Vedānta, avidyā (nescience) is the beginningless ignorance that veils Brahman and projects the world of multiplicity; its nature as neither real nor unreal (anirvacanīya), its locus, and its removal through brahma-jñāna are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Āgamic Tradition
concept.description: The Āgamic (Tantric) tradition: the Śaiva Āgamas (28 principal texts), Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātras and Vaikhānasas, Śākta Tantras; their structure (jñāna, yoga, kriyā, caryā), their role in temple ritual, iconography, and initiation (dīkṣā); their distinction from Vedic orthopraxy and their integration into Smārta tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Āgamic (Tantric) tradition: the Śaiva Āgamas (28 principal texts), Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātras and Vaikhānasas, Śākta Tantras; their structure (jñāna, yoga, kriyā, caryā), their role in temple ritual, iconography, and initiation (dīkṣā); their distinction from Vedic orthopraxy and their integration into Smārta tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Alaṅkāra Śāstra
concept.description: The Sanskrit poetics tradition analyzing figures of speech (alaṅkāras), poetic merits (guṇas), and aesthetic defects (doṣas); its major texts and theorists are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The Sanskrit poetics tradition analyzing figures of speech (alaṅkāras), poetic merits (guṇas), and aesthetic defects (doṣas); its major texts and theorists are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Anubandha Catuṣṭaya
concept.description: The four preliminary factors traditionally stated at the beginning of a Vedānta work: adhikārin (qualified student), viṣaya (subject), prayojana (purpose), and sambandha (relationship).
concept.body: The four preliminary factors traditionally stated at the beginning of a Vedānta work: adhikārin (qualified student), viṣaya (subject), prayojana (purpose), and sambandha (relationship).

concept.title: Āpaddharma
concept.description: The Dharmaśāstra concept of āpaddharma (dharma in times of distress/emergency): the relaxation of normal rules for survival, the hierarchy of permissible actions, and the principle that normal dharma resumes when the emergency passes; its textual basis in Manusmṛti and other Smṛtis is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Dharmaśāstra concept of āpaddharma (dharma in times of distress/emergency): the relaxation of normal rules for survival, the hierarchy of permissible actions, and the principle that normal dharma resumes when the emergency passes; its textual basis in Manusmṛti and other Smṛtis is represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Apparatus Criticus
concept.description: The critical apparatus in a scholarly edition recording variant readings, editorial decisions, and conjectures; its formats (positive, negative, hybrid) are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The critical apparatus in a scholarly edition recording variant readings, editorial decisions, and conjectures; its formats (positive, negative, hybrid) are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Arjuna
concept.description: The third Pāṇḍava, renowned archer and recipient of the Bhagavad Gītā; traditional narratives and textual portrayals are represented without historical conflation.
concept.body: The third Pāṇḍava, renowned archer and recipient of the Bhagavad Gītā; traditional narratives and textual portrayals are represented without historical conflation.

concept.title: Artha
concept.description: One of the four puruṣārthas, referring to material prosperity, power, and security; its pursuit is contextualized by dharma in textual traditions.
concept.body: One of the four puruṣārthas, referring to material prosperity, power, and security; its pursuit is contextualized by dharma in textual traditions.

concept.title: Āśrama Dharma
concept.description: The four āśramas (stages of life) in Dharmaśāstra: brahmacarya (student), gṛhastha (householder), vānaprastha (forest-dweller), and saṃnyāsa (renunciant); their duties (dharma), transitions (saṃskāras), and the ideal progression toward mokṣa are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The four āśramas (stages of life) in Dharmaśāstra: brahmacarya (student), gṛhastha (householder), vānaprastha (forest-dweller), and saṃnyāsa (renunciant); their duties (dharma), transitions (saṃskāras), and the ideal progression toward mokṣa are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Āśrama
concept.description: The four-stage model of life—brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha, saṃnyāsa—whose applicability and interpretation vary across texts and historical periods.
concept.body: The four-stage model of life—brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha, saṃnyāsa—whose applicability and interpretation vary across texts and historical periods.

concept.title: Atharvaveda Śākhās
concept.description: The recensions (śākhās) of the Atharvaveda: Śaunaka (the principal surviving recension) and Paippalāda (partially preserved in Kashmir and Orissa); their textual differences and the Atharvaveda's unique character among the four Vedas are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The recensions (śākhās) of the Atharvaveda: Śaunaka (the principal surviving recension) and Paippalāda (partially preserved in Kashmir and Orissa); their textual differences and the Atharvaveda's unique character among the four Vedas are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Ātman
concept.description: A term for the self or innermost principle whose nature and relationship to Brahman constitute a central question in Upaniṣadic and Vedāntic thought.
concept.body: A term for the self or innermost principle whose nature and relationship to Brahman constitute a central question in Upaniṣadic and Vedāntic thought.

concept.title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapters
concept.description: The eighteen adhyāyas (chapters) of the Bhagavad Gītā, their thematic progression from viṣāda-yoga to mokṣa-sannyāsa-yoga, and their philosophical themes (karma-yoga, jñāna-yoga, bhakti-yoga) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The eighteen adhyāyas (chapters) of the Bhagavad Gītā, their thematic progression from viṣāda-yoga to mokṣa-sannyāsa-yoga, and their philosophical themes (karma-yoga, jñāna-yoga, bhakti-yoga) are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Bhagavad Gītā Philosophy
concept.description: The philosophical teachings of the Bhagavad Gītā: the synthesis of karma-yoga (selfless action), jñāna-yoga (knowledge), and bhakti-yoga (devotion); the nature of the self (ātman), the supreme (puruṣottama), the three guṇas, and the concept of svadharma; its influence on later Vedānta schools are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The philosophical teachings of the Bhagavad Gītā: the synthesis of karma-yoga (selfless action), jñāna-yoga (knowledge), and bhakti-yoga (devotion); the nature of the self (ātman), the supreme (puruṣottama), the three guṇas, and the concept of svadharma; its influence on later Vedānta schools are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Bhakti Movement
concept.description: The Bhakti movement (7th–17th centuries): the devotional renaissance across India emphasizing personal devotion (bhakti) to a chosen deity (iṣṭa-devatā) over ritual orthodoxy; its poet-saints (Āḻvārs, Nāyanārs, Vārkarīs, Haridāsas, Rāmānanda, Kabīr, Tulsīdās, Mīrābāī, Sūrdās, Caitanya); its vernacular literature, social egalitarianism, and lasting impact on Hindu practice are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Bhakti movement (7th–17th centuries): the devotional renaissance across India emphasizing personal devotion (bhakti) to a chosen deity (iṣṭa-devatā) over ritual orthodoxy; its poet-saints (Āḻvārs, Nāyanārs, Vārkarīs, Haridāsas, Rāmānanda, Kabīr, Tulsīdās, Mīrābāī, Sūrdās, Caitanya); its vernacular literature, social egalitarianism, and lasting impact on Hindu practice are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Bhakti
concept.description: Devotional orientation or practice whose objects, methods, and theological frameworks vary widely across texts, traditions, and historical periods.
concept.body: Devotional orientation or practice whose objects, methods, and theological frameworks vary widely across texts, traditions, and historical periods.

concept.title: Bharatanatyam Repertoire
concept.description: The traditional Bharatanatyam performance repertoire (mārgam): alarippu (invocation), jatisvaram (pure dance), śabdam (lyric dance), varṇam (centerpiece), padam (abhinaya), tillāṇa (finale), and ślokam/maṅgalam (conclusion); the role of nattuvanār, the mridangam, violin, and flute accompaniment are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The traditional Bharatanatyam performance repertoire (mārgam): alarippu (invocation), jatisvaram (pure dance), śabdam (lyric dance), varṇam (centerpiece), padam (abhinaya), tillāṇa (finale), and ślokam/maṅgalam (conclusion); the role of nattuvanār, the mridangam, violin, and flute accompaniment are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Bhedābheda Avibhāga-bheda
concept.description: The Bhedābheda doctrine of avibhāga-bheda (difference-in-non-difference), asserting that the whole and its parts are simultaneously different and non-different (like fire and its sparks); its variants in Bhāskara, Yādavaprakāśa, and Nimbārka are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Bhedābheda doctrine of avibhāga-bheda (difference-in-non-difference), asserting that the whole and its parts are simultaneously different and non-different (like fire and its sparks); its variants in Bhāskara, Yādavaprakāśa, and Nimbārka are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Bhedābheda
concept.description: The "difference and non-difference" doctrine, positing that the individual self and Brahman are simultaneously distinct and non-distinct; foundational for Viśiṣṭādvaita and other schools.
concept.body: The "difference and non-difference" doctrine, positing that the individual self and Brahman are simultaneously distinct and non-distinct; foundational for Viśiṣṭādvaita and other schools.

concept.title: Bhīṣma
concept.description: The grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, known for his vow of celibacy and role in the Mahābhārata; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.
concept.body: The grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, known for his vow of celibacy and role in the Mahābhārata; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.

concept.title: Brahman
concept.description: The ultimate reality or ground of being in Vedāntic traditions, described through both negation (neti neti) and positive affirmation depending on the school.
concept.body: The ultimate reality or ground of being in Vedāntic traditions, described through both negation (neti neti) and positive affirmation depending on the school.

concept.title: Carnatic Rāga System
concept.description: The Carnatic rāga system: the 72 melakartā (parent) rāgas organized in the kaṭapayādi formula, their janya (derived) rāgas; the rāga structure (ārohaṇa/avarohaṇa), the gamaka (ornamentation), and the role of rāga in conveying rasa (emotion) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Carnatic rāga system: the 72 melakartā (parent) rāgas organized in the kaṭapayādi formula, their janya (derived) rāgas; the rāga structure (ārohaṇa/avarohaṇa), the gamaka (ornamentation), and the role of rāga in conveying rasa (emotion) are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Camakam
concept.description: The Camakam, the second part of the Śrī Rudram (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.7), listing the desired boons for the yajamāna; its repetitive structure (ca me) and ritual use alongside the Namakam are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Camakam, the second part of the Śrī Rudram (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.7), listing the desired boons for the yajamāna; its repetitive structure (ca me) and ritual use alongside the Namakam are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Chandas
concept.description: The Vedāṅga of metre and prosody, governing the rhythmic structure of Vedic and classical Sanskrit verse.
concept.body: The Vedāṅga of metre and prosody, governing the rhythmic structure of Vedic and classical Sanskrit verse.

concept.title: Codicology
concept.description: The study of manuscripts as physical objects: materials, structure, binding, layout, and production; its methods and descriptive standards are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The study of manuscripts as physical objects: materials, structure, binding, layout, and production; its methods and descriptive standards are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Collation
concept.description: The systematic comparison of manuscript witnesses to record variant readings; its methods (manual, mechanical, digital) and output formats are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The systematic comparison of manuscript witnesses to record variant readings; its methods (manual, mechanical, digital) and output formats are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Colophon
concept.description: The concluding note in a manuscript recording scribe, date, place, patron, or other production details; its formulaic variations across traditions are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The concluding note in a manuscript recording scribe, date, place, patron, or other production details; its formulaic variations across traditions are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Critical Edition
concept.description: The scholarly reconstruction of a text from multiple manuscript witnesses, applying textual criticism to establish the most probable original reading; its methods and principles are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The scholarly reconstruction of a text from multiple manuscript witnesses, applying textual criticism to establish the most probable original reading; its methods and principles are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Dāna Types
concept.description: The classification of dāna (gift) in Dharmaśāstra: nitya (daily), naimittika (occasional), kāmya (desire-motivated), and vimukti (liberation-oriented); the qualified recipients (supātra), objects, and occasions for giving are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The classification of dāna (gift) in Dharmaśāstra: nitya (daily), naimittika (occasional), kāmya (desire-motivated), and vimukti (liberation-oriented); the qualified recipients (supātra), objects, and occasions for giving are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Dāna
concept.description: The practice of giving or gift-giving, regulated in Dharmaśāstra by donor, recipient, gift-type, and occasion; a key householder duty.
concept.body: The practice of giving or gift-giving, regulated in Dharmaśāstra by donor, recipient, gift-type, and occasion; a key householder duty.

concept.title: Darśana
concept.description: Darśana (auspicious sight): the act of beholding a deity, guru, or sacred object in Hindu practice; its theological significance as a two-way exchange of grace (the deity sees the devotee, the devotee sees the deity); its role in temple worship, pilgrimage (tīrtha-yātrā), and guru-seva are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
Darśana (auspicious sight): the act of beholding a deity, guru, or sacred object in Hindu practice; its theological significance as a two-way exchange of grace (the deity sees the devotee, the devotee sees the deity); its role in temple worship, pilgrimage (tīrtha-yātrā), and guru-seva are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Dharma
concept.description: A foundational concept whose meanings include duty, law, virtue, and the inherent nature of things; its specific sense depends on textual and situational context.
concept.body: A foundational concept whose meanings include duty, law, virtue, and the inherent nature of things; its specific sense depends on textual and situational context.

concept.title: Dharmasūtra
concept.description: The earliest genre of Dharma literature, composed in sūtra style and associated with Vedic schools; distinct from the later metrical Smṛtis.
concept.body: The earliest genre of Dharma literature, composed in sūtra style and associated with Vedic schools; distinct from the later metrical Smṛtis.

concept.title: Digital Humanities
concept.description: The interdisciplinary field applying computational methods to humanities research; its Indian studies projects, text analysis, and infrastructure are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The interdisciplinary field applying computational methods to humanities research; its Indian studies projects, text analysis, and infrastructure are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Digitization
concept.description: The process of creating digital surrogates of manuscripts (imaging, metadata, OCR/HTR); its standards (FADGI, Metamorfoze), workflows, and access models are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The process of creating digital surrogates of manuscripts (imaging, metadata, OCR/HTR); its standards (FADGI, Metamorfoze), workflows, and access models are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Draupadī
concept.description: The wife of the five Pāṇḍavas, central to the Mahābhārata narrative; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.
concept.body: The wife of the five Pāṇḍavas, central to the Mahābhārata narrative; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.

concept.title: Durgā Forms
concept.description: The forms of Durgā: the nine Navadurgās (Śailaputrī, Brahmacāriṇī, Chandraghaṇṭā, Kūṣmāṇḍā, Skandamātā, Kātyāyanī, Kālarātrī, Mahāgaurī, Siddhidātrī); the ten Mahāvidyās; the warrior Caṇḍikā and the mother Ambikā; their iconography, the Devī Māhātmya narrative, and the Navarātri festival are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Durgā
concept.description: A form of the Goddess with major textual, ritual, and festival presence; represented here without imposing a single theological interpretation across Śākta traditions.
concept.body: A form of the Goddess with major textual, ritual, and festival presence; represented here without imposing a single theological interpretation across Śākta traditions.

concept.title: Duryodhana
concept.description: The eldest Kaurava and primary antagonist of the Mahābhārata war; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.
concept.body: The eldest Kaurava and primary antagonist of the Mahābhārata war; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.

concept.title: Dvaita Pañca-bheda
concept.description: The Dvaita Vedānta doctrine of five eternal differences (pañca-bheda): between Brahman (Viṣṇu) and jīva, between Brahman and jagat, between jīva and jīva, between jīva and jagat, and between jagat and jagat; their epistemic and ontological status are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Dvaita Vedānta doctrine of five eternal differences (pañca-bheda): between Brahman (Viṣṇu) and jīva, between Brahman and jagat, between jīva and jīva, between jīva and jagat, and between jagat and jagat; their epistemic and ontological status are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Dvaita Sākṣi-bhāva
concept.description: In Dvaita Vedānta, the sākṣi-bhāva (witness-consciousness) of the jīva is its capacity to witness its own mental states while remaining distinct from them; its role in self-knowledge and liberation is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
In Dvaita Vedānta, the sākṣi-bhāva (witness-consciousness) of the jīva is its capacity to witness its own mental states while remaining distinct from them; its role in self-knowledge and liberation is represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Emendation
concept.description: An editorial correction proposed where all manuscript witnesses appear corrupt; its justification, notation, and scholarly conventions are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: An editorial correction proposed where all manuscript witnesses appear corrupt; its justification, notation, and scholarly conventions are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Epigraphy
concept.description: The study of inscriptions on durable materials (stone, metal, copper plates) for historical, linguistic, and cultural reconstruction; its methods and Indian corpora are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The study of inscriptions on durable materials (stone, metal, copper plates) for historical, linguistic, and cultural reconstruction; its methods and Indian corpora are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Folio
concept.description: A single leaf of a manuscript (two pages: recto and verso); its numbering, structure, and descriptive conventions are represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: A single leaf of a manuscript (two pages: recto and verso); its numbering, structure, and descriptive conventions are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Gāndhārī
concept.description: The wife of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and mother of the Kauravas, known for her voluntary blindness; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.
concept.body: The wife of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and mother of the Kauravas, known for her voluntary blindness; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.

concept.title: Gaṇeśa Forms
concept.description: The forms of Gaṇeśa: Bāl Gaṇeśa, Taruṇa Gaṇeśa, Bhakti Gaṇeśa, Vīra Gaṇeśa, Śakti Gaṇeśa, Dvija Gaṇeśa, Siddhi Gaṇeśa, Ucchiṣṭa Gaṇeśa, Vighna Gaṇeśa, Kṣipra Gaṇeśa, Heramba Gaṇeśa, and Lakṣmī Gaṇeśa; their iconographic variations and the thirty-two forms tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The forms of Gaṇeśa: Bāl Gaṇeśa, Taruṇa Gaṇeśa, Bhakti Gaṇeśa, Vīra Gaṇeśa, Śakti Gaṇeśa, Dvija Gaṇeśa, Siddhi Gaṇeśa, Ucchiṣṭa Gaṇeśa, Vighna Gaṇeśa, Kṣipra Gaṇeśa, Heramba Gaṇeśa, and Lakṣmī Gaṇeśa; their iconographic variations and the thirty-two forms tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Gāyatrī Mantra
concept.description: The Gāyatrī Mantra (Ṛgveda 3.62.10), addressed to Savitṛ, is the most revered Vedic mantra; its metre (gāyatrī), traditional initiation (upadeśa), and role in sandhyāvandana are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Gāyatrī Mantra (Ṛgveda 3.62.10), addressed to Savitṛ, is the most revered Vedic mantra; its metre (gāyatrī), traditional initiation (upadeśa), and role in sandhyāvandana are represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Gāyatrī
concept.description: A celebrated Vedic metre and the hymn composed in it (Ṛgveda 3.62.10); also personified as a deity in later traditions.
concept.body: A celebrated Vedic metre and the hymn composed in it (Ṛgveda 3.62.10); also personified as a deity in later traditions.

concept.title: Gītā Bhakti-yoga
concept.description: The Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of bhakti-yoga (the yoga of devotion): the qualities of the devotee (bhakta), the nature of divine love, and the supremacy of bhakti as the path to liberation; its exposition across chapters 7–12 and 18 is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of bhakti-yoga (the yoga of devotion): the qualities of the devotee (bhakta), the nature of divine love, and the supremacy of bhakti as the path to liberation; its exposition across chapters 7–12 and 18 is represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Gītā Dhyāna
concept.description: The traditional meditative verses recited before studying the Bhagavad Gītā, invoking the text and its lineage; represented here as a catalogue entry.
concept.body: The traditional meditative verses recited before studying the Bhagavad Gītā, invoking the text and its lineage; represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Gītā Jñāna-yoga
concept.description: The Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of jñāna-yoga (the yoga of knowledge): the distinction between kṣetra (field) and kṣetrajña (knower of the field), the nature of the self (ātman), and the realization of brahman; its exposition across chapters 13–18 is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of jñāna-yoga (the yoga of knowledge): the distinction between kṣetra (field) and kṣetrajña (knower of the field), the nature of the self (ātman), and the realization of brahman; its exposition across chapters 13–18 is represented here as a catalogue entry.
---

concept.title: Gītā Karma-yoga
concept.description: The Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of karma-yoga (the yoga of selfless action): niṣkāma-karma (action without attachment to fruits), svadharma (one's own duty), and the synthesis of action and knowledge; its exposition across chapters 2–5 is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
concept.body:
The Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of karma-yoga (the yoga of selfless action): niṣkāma-karma (action without attachment to fruits), svadharma (one's own duty), and the synthesis of action and knowledge; its exposition across chapters 2–5 is represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Nyāya Īśvara
concept.description: The Nyāya concept of Īśvara (God) as the efficient cause (nimitta-kāraṇa) of the universe, the creator, sustainer, and destroyer of the world, who is distinct from the material cause (prakṛti) and the individual selves (jīva); the arguments for God's existence (kārya-kāraṇa-anvaya, āyojanāt, dhṛtyādēḥ, padāt, pratyayataḥ, śrutēḥ) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Nyāya Pramāṇas
concept.description: The Nyāya school recognizes four pramāṇas (means of valid knowledge): pratyakṣa (perception), anumāna (inference), upamāna (comparison), and śabda (verbal testimony); their definitions, scope, and interrelations are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Nyāya Siddhānta
concept.description: The Nyāya school's core doctrines: the sixteen padārthas (categories) including pramāṇa (means of knowledge), prameya (objects of knowledge), saṃśaya (doubt), prayojana (purpose), dṛṣṭānta (example), siddhānta (tenet), avayava (members of inference), tarka (reasoning), nirṇaya (ascertainment), vāda (discussion), jalpa (wrangling), vitaṇḍā (cavil), hetvābhāsa (fallacies), chala (quibble), jāti (futile objection), and nigrahasthāna (point of defeat); their interrelations and epistemic significance are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: The five great elements (pañcamahābhūta) in Vedic and Sāṃkhya cosmology: ākāśa (space/ether), vāyu (air), agni (fire), jala/ap (water), pṛthvī (earth); their subtle essences (tanmātras: śabda, sparśa, rūpa, rasa, gandha), their sequence of manifestation, and their correspondence to sense organs are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: The doctrine of "real transformation" — the world as a genuine modification (pariṇāma) of Brahman or prakṛti, upheld by Viśiṣṭādvaita, Dvaita, and Sāṃkhya.

concept.title: Prāyaścitta Types
concept.description: The classification of prāyaścitta (expiation) in Dharmaśātra: prāṇāyāma, tīrtha-yātrā, dāna, vrata, homa, japa, and fasting; their application to specific offenses (pātaka, upapātaka) and the gradation of penances are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Pūjā Ṣoḍaśopacāra
concept.description: The sixteen upacāras (offerings) in formal Pūjā: āvāhana (invocation), āsana (seat), pādyā (water for feet), arghya (water for hands), ācamana (sipping water), snāna (bath), vastra (clothing), yajñopavīta (sacred thread), gandha (sandalwood), puṣpa (flowers), dhūpa (incense), dīpa (lamp), naivedya (food), tāmbūla (betel), nīrājana (waving lights), and mantra-puṣpāñjali; their sequence and significance are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: The five distinguishing characteristics of a Purāṇa: sarga (creation), pratisarga (re-creation), vaṃśa (genealogy), manvantara (cosmic ages), and vaṃśānucarita (dynastic history).

concept.title: Purāṇa Sectarian Classification
concept.description: The traditional tripartite classification of Purāṇas by predominance of guṇas: Sāttvika (Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa), Rājasa (Brahmā), and Tāmasa (Śiva); this classification's textual basis and sectarian implications are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Purāṇa Structure
concept.description: The five characteristic topics (pañcalakṣaṇa) of the Purāṇas: sarga (creation), pratisarga (secondary creation), vaṃśa (genealogies), manvantara (cosmic cycles), and vaṃśānucarita (dynastic histories); their textual manifestation across the Purāṇic corpus is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Rājadharma

concept.title: Rāma Forms
concept.description: The forms of Rāma: the prince of Ayodhyā, the exiled forest-dweller, the victor over Rāvaṇa, the ideal king (Rāmarājya), and the supreme Parabrahman (in Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa); his iconography (bow, arrow, accompanied by Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, Hanumān), and his worship in the Rāmānandī and Rāmānuja traditions are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Saṃskāra Types

concept.title: Sāṃkhya Evolution (Parinama)
concept.description: The Sāṃkhya theory of cosmic evolution (pariṇāma) from prakṛti: the sequential manifestation of mahat (buddhi), ahaṃkāra (ego), the five tanmātras (subtle elements), the five mahābhūtas (gross elements), the five jñānendriyas (sense organs), the five karmendriyas (action organs), and manas (mind); the teleological direction of evolution toward the liberation of puruṣa is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Sāṃkhya Guṇatraya
concept.description: The three guṇas (sattva, rajas, tamas) as the constituent strands of prakṛti in Sāṃkhya philosophy; their characteristics, interactions, and role in cosmic evolution and bondage are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Sāṃkhya Puruṣa-Prakṛti
concept.description: The Sāṃkhya dualism of puruṣa (pure consciousness, plural, passive witness) and prakṛti (primordial matter, singular, active, composed of three guṇas); their interaction (saṃyoga) as the cause of evolution, the distinction between knowledge (jñāna) and ignorance (ajñāna), and liberation (kaivalya) as the isolation of puruṣa from prakṛti are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Sāṃkhya Tattvas
concept.description: The Sāṃkhya enumeration of twenty-five tattvas (principles): prakṛti (primordial matter), mahat (buddhi), ahaṃkāra, five tanmātras, five mahābhūtas, five jñānendriyas, five karmendriyas, manas, and puruṣa (consciousness); their evolutionary sequence and interrelations are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Saṃnyāsa
concept.description: Saṃnyāsa (renunciation): the fourth āśrama (stage of life) in Dharmaśāstra, characterized by the renunciation of worldly duties, the adoption of the ochre robe (kāṣāya), the begging bowl (bhikṣāpātra), and the pursuit of mokṣa through jñāna and vairāgya; the types of saṃnyāsa (kuṭīcaka, bahūdaka, haṃsa, paramahaṃsa), the saṃnyāsa dīkṣā, and the saṃnyāsī's daily routine are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Saptarṣi
concept.description: The Saptarṣi (seven sages): the seven primordial sages (Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vasiṣṭha) who are the mind-born sons of Brahmā, the authors of Vedic hymns, and the progenitors of gotras; their astronomical identification with the Ursa Major constellation (Saptarṣi Maṇḍala) and their role in Vedic tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Sarasvatī Forms
concept.description: The forms of Sarasvatī: Vāc (speech), Bhāratī (eloquence), Śāradā (autumn goddess), and Vāṇī (voice); her iconography with vīṇā, pustaka, and haṃsa, and her role as goddess of knowledge, arts, and learning are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: A goddess associated with learning, speech, and the arts; also the name of a Vedic river whose identification is debated in scholarship and tradition.

concept.title: Śaunaka Śākhā
concept.description: The Śaunaka Śākhā is the principal surviving recension of the Atharvaveda; its texts include the Atharvaveda Saṃhitā, Gopatha Brāhmaṇa, and several Upaniṣads; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Śaiva Āgamas
concept.description: The twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas (e.g., Kāmika, Kāraṇa, Suprabheda, Raurava, Mṛgendra, Sarvokta, Pārameśvara, Kiraṇa, Vātula, Parameśvara) and their upāgamas; their fourfold structure (jñāna, yoga, kriyā, caryā), their doctrine of Śiva-Śakti, the pāśa (bondage) and mokṣa; their role in temple construction, daily worship, and initiation are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: The Vedāṅga concerned with phonetics, pronunciation, and euphonic combination; its treatises form the foundation for Vedic recitation.

concept.title: Śilpa Śāstra
concept.description: The traditional Indian system of iconography and sculpture, prescribing proportions, gestures, attributes, and materials for deity images; its texts and regional schools are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Śrāddha Types
concept.description: The types of śrāddha (ancestral rites) in Dharmaśāstra: nitya (daily), naimittika (occasional), kāmya (desire-motivated), and the specific rites like sapiṇḍīkaraṇa, saparvaṇa, ekodiṣṭa; their performers, timing, and offerings are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Śruti
concept.description: Śruti (that which is heard): the authoritative revealed texts of Hinduism, comprising the four Vedas (Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma, Atharva) and their associated Brāhmaṇas, Āraṇyakas, and Upaniṣads; distinguished from Smṛti (remembered tradition); its apauruṣeya (non-human authorship) status, its role as the ultimate pramāṇa in orthodox schools, and its oral transmission (paramparā) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Śuddhādvaita Puṣṭi
concept.description: In Śuddhādvaita Vedānta (Vallabha), puṣṭi (grace) is the unmerited divine favor that enables the soul's participation in Kṛṣṇa's līlā; the puṣṭi-mārga (path of grace) and its distinction from the maryādā-mārga (path of law) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: A conventional symbol or abbreviation identifying a specific manuscript witness in a critical apparatus; its assignment and notation standards are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Sītā
concept.description: The wife of Rāma, central to the Rāmāyaṇa; traditional narratives are represented without historical conflation.

concept.title: Smṛti
concept.description: Smṛti (that which is remembered): the body of post-Vedic authoritative texts including the Dharmaśāstras (Manusmṛti, Yājñavalkyasmṛti), the Itihāsas (Mahābhārata, Rāmāyaṇa), the Purāṇas, the Āgamas, and the Vedāṅgas; distinguished from Śruti (revealed) as being of human authorship but traditionally authoritative; its role in prescribing dharma, ritual, and social order is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Śrīmad Bhāgavata Commentary Traditions
concept.description: The diverse commentarial traditions on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, including Śrīdhara Svāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, and others; represented as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Stemmatics
concept.description: The method of reconstructing manuscript genealogies (stemma codicum) to infer textual relationships; its principles, limitations, and computational approaches are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Strīdharmā
concept.description: The body of Dharmaśāstra prescriptions concerning women's duties and rites; textual prescriptions are distinguished from diverse historical and regional practices.

concept.title: Sūrya Navagraha
concept.description: Sūrya as the chief of the Navagraha (nine planets), his iconography (seven-horse chariot, Aruṇa as charioteer), the Sūrya mantras, and his role in Vedic and Jyotiṣa traditions are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Taittirīya Śākhā
concept.description: The Taittirīya Śākhā is the principal surviving recension of the Kṛṣṇa (Black) Yajurveda, prevalent in South India; its texts include the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, Brāhmaṇa, Āraṇyaka, and Upaniṣad; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Tantra Śāstra
concept.description: The Tantra Śāstra corpus: the textual tradition of Tantra (Śākta, Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava, Buddhist), characterized by ritual (kriyā), meditation (yoga), mantra, yantra, maṇḍala, and the guru-śiṣya transmission; its distinction from Vedic orthopraxy (smārta), its esoteric (guhya) nature, and its influence on temple ritual, iconography, and popular practice are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Tantra
concept.description: Tantra: the esoteric ritual and yogic tradition transmitted through guru-śiṣya lineages, characterized by the use of mantra, yantra, maṇḍala, dīkṣā (initiation), and the worship of deities in their fierce and benign forms; its textual corpus (Tantras, Āgamas, Saṃhitās), its distinction from Vedic smārta practice, and its influence on temple ritual, iconography, and popular practice are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Textual Criticism
concept.description: The discipline of evaluating manuscript variants to reconstruct a text's history and establish an edited text; its methods (stemmatics, best-text, cladistics) are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Thumri and Dadra
concept.description: The light classical forms of Hindustani music: thumrī (romantic, erotic, based on Braj/Hindi poetry, set to dīpacandī/punjabi tāl), dadra (lighter, faster, in dadra tāl), kājrī, caitī, horī; their gharanā styles (Purab, Punjab), their place in the concert format after khayāl, and their emotive (śṛṅgāra) content are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Tīrtha Types
concept.description: The classification of tīrtha (pilgrimage sites) in Purāṇic and Dharmaśāstra tradition: deva-tīrtha (deity-associated), ṛṣi-tīrtha (sage-associated), mṛtyu-tīrtha (death-related), and the distinction between mukti-tīrtha (liberation-granting) and bhukti-tīrtha (enjoyment-granting); their ritual protocols are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Trisandhyā
concept.description: The trisandhyā (three daily junctions): the Vedic prescription for worship at dawn (prātaḥ-sandhyā), noon (mādhyāhnika), and dusk (sāyaṃ-sandhyā); the Gāyatrī mantra recitation, prāṇāyāma, arghya offering, and upasthāna; its role in the daily routine of the twice-born (dvija) and its continuation in modern practice are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Vairāgya
concept.description: Dispassion or non-attachment, presented in texts as a prerequisite for contemplative progress, with degrees and nuances described differently across traditions.

concept.title: Vaiśeṣika Atomism
concept.description: The Vaiśeṣika atomic theory positing four kinds of eternal, indivisible atoms (paramāṇu) — earth, water, fire, air — each with distinct qualities (guṇa); their binary combinations (dvyanuka) and ternary combinations (tryanuka) forming the gross physical world; the theory's differences from Greek atomism and its role in Vaiśeṣika physics are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

---

concept.title: Vaiśeṣika Creation Theory
concept.description: The Vaiśeṣika theory of creation (sṛṣṭi) and dissolution (pralaya) through the combination and separation of eternal atoms (paramāṇu) guided by the unseen force (adṛṣṭa) of individual selves; the atomic structure of the four physical elements (earth, water, fire, air) and the non-atomic substances (space, time, direction, mind, self) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Vaiśeṣika Padārthas
concept.description: The Vaiśeṣika school enumerates seven padārthas (categories of existence): dravya (substance), guṇa (quality), karma (action), sāmānya (generality), viśeṣa (particularity), samavāya (inherence), and abhāva (absence); their definitions and interrelations are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Vaiśeṣika Paramāṇu
concept.description: The Vaiśeṣika atomic theory (paramāṇu-vāda) positing eternal, indivisible atoms as the ultimate constituents of physical substances; its metaphysical implications and differences from other atomic theories are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Vaiṣṇava Āgamas
concept.description: The Vaiṣṇava Āgamas: the Pāñcarātra corpus (e.g., Jayākhya, Ahirbudhnya, Paushkara, Sāttvata) and the Vaikhānasa texts; their doctrine of Viṣṇu's five forms (para, vyūha, vibhava, antaryāmin, arcā), the fivefold daily worship (pañcakāla), and their influence on temple ritual in Śrīvaiṣṇava and other traditions are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Varṇa-āśrama Dharma
concept.description: The integrated system of varṇa (four social classes) and āśrama (four life stages) duties in Dharmaśāstra; the interdependence of social and life-stage obligations, their textual basis in Smṛti texts, and their role in traditional society are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Vedic Metre (Chandas)

concept.title: Vedic Ritual (Yajña)

concept.title: Yoga Aṣṭāṅga
concept.description: The eight limbs (aṣṭāṅga) of Patañjali's Yoga: yama (restraints), niyama (observances), āsana (posture), prāṇāyāma (breath control), pratyāhāra (sense withdrawal), dhāraṇā (concentration), dhyāna (meditation), samādhi (absorption); their sequential practice and interdependence are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Yoga Kleśas

concept.description: Yoga Nidrā (yogic sleep): a guided relaxation and meditation technique leading to a state of conscious deep sleep between waking and sleeping; its roots in the tantric tradition (nyāsa), its modern systematization (Satyananda Saraswati), and its therapeutic applications are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Yoga Samādhi

concept.title: Karnāṭaka Saṅgīta
concept.description: Karnāṭaka Saṅgīta (कर्नाटक संगीत / கர்நாடக சங்கீதம் / കർണാടക സംഗീതం), the classical music tradition of South India (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana). Core: rāga (melodic framework), tāḷa (rhythmic cycle), and compositional forms — varṇam, kṛti, tillāṇa, javali, padam, svarajati. The Trinity (18th-19th c.): Tyāgarāja (kṛti perfection, bhakti), Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar (Sanskrit, śrī vidyā, western notes), Śyāma Śāstri (Svarajati, Kāmākṣi). Pedagogy: sarali varisai, jaṇṭai varisai, daṭṭu varisai, alankāram, gītaṃ, svarajati, varṇam, kṛti. The 72 melakarta rāga system (Venkatamakhin). Instruments: vīṇā, veṇu, violin, mṛdaṅgam, ghaṭam, kanjira, morsing. The December Music Season (Chennai) is the world's largest classical music festival. --- The classical music tradition of South India, with its rāga, tāḷa, and compositional forms (kṛti, varṇam, tillāṇa); its history, composers (Tyāgarāja, Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar, Śyāma Śāstri), and pedagogy are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Kāṭhakaḷi
concept.description: Kāṭhakaḷi (കഥകളി), Kerala's classical dance-drama (17th century synthesis of Kṛṣṇanāṭṭam, Rāmanāṭṭam, and folk traditions). Key elements: elaborate vesham (makeup/costume) — paccā (green, noble), kaṭṭi (knife, anti-hero), kari (black, demoness), taṭi (beard: white=divine, red=evil, black=hunter), minukku (radiant, female/sage); the navarasas (nine emotions) through facial muscles (netrābhinaya); the āṭṭakathās (scripts) from Mahābhārata, Rāmāyaṇa, Bhāgavata (e.g., Nalacaritam, Kalyāṇasaugandhikam); sopāna-saṅgīta (Sopana music) with ceṇḍa, maṭalam, elathāḷam; rigorous gurukula training (8-10 years) at Kala Mandalam, Kottakkal. Recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. A synthesis of nṛtya (dance), nṛtta (pure movement), and nāṭya (drama). --- The classical dance-drama tradition of Kerala, with elaborate costume, makeup, and facial expressions; its repertoire (āṭṭakathās), music, and training system are represented here as a catalogue entry.

concept.title: Mohiniyāṭṭam
concept.description: Mohiniyāṭṭam (മോഹിനിയാട്ടം), Kerala's classical solo dance (lasya style), traditionally performed by women. Reconstructed in the 1930s by V.N. Menon and Kala Mandalam (Vallathol Narayana Menon, Mukundraj). Key elements: graceful circular movements (cuzhippu), swaying gait (gamana), subtle facial expressions (sāttvika abhinaya), white/cream costume with gold border (kasavu), jasmine hair adornment. The repertoire: colkeṭṭu (invocation), jati-svaram, varṇam, padam, tillānā. Music: Sopana style, Carnatic rāgas (Tōḍi, Bhairavi, Kalyāṇi), accompaniment: veena, veṇu, maddaḷam, eḷattāḷam. Themes: Śṛṅgāra (love), Bhakti (devotion to Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa). Mohinī = Viṣṇu's enchantress form (distributing amṛta). Recognized by Sangeet Natak Akademi. --- The classical solo dance tradition of Kerala, characterized by graceful circular movements and feminine expression; its repertoire and historical reconstruction are represented here as a catalogue entry.

deity.title: Ayyappan
deity.description: Ayyappan (അയ്യപ്പന്‍ / ஐயப்பன்), also Śāstā, Hariharaputra, Dharma-Śāstā — the deity of Sabarimala, born from the union of Śiva and Viṣṇu (as Mohinī). Embodies the synthesis of Śaiva and Vaiṣṇava traditions. Key attributes: celibacy (naiṣṭhika brahmacarya), the 18 holy steps (paṭinēṭṭāmpaṭi / பதினெட்டாம்படி), the 41-day vrata (maṇḍala kālam / மண்டல காலம்) with strict observances (black/blue clothes, no shaving, brahmacarya, daily bath). The pilgrimage to Sabarimala (Kerala) draws 40-50 million annually (Nov-Jan). The Makaravilakku (Makara Jyoti) on Makara Saṅkrānti is the climax. Worshipped across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and beyond. The Vāvaru (Muslim devotee) shrine at Erumeli exemplifies communal harmony. ---

deity.description: Devī (देवी / தேவி / ਦੇਵੀ / ദേവি / দেবী), the Goddess, Śakti, Ambikā, Durgā, Pārvatī, Kālī, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Mahiṣāsuramardinī, Caṇḍikā, Annapūrṇā, Kāmākṣī, Mīnākṣī. Central to Śākta traditions (Śrīvidyā, Kālikā, Durgā Pūjā). The Devī Māhātmya (Durgā Saptashatī, Caṇḍī-pāṭha) is the foundational text. Manifestations: Navadurgā (9 forms), Daśamahāvidyā (10 wisdom goddesses), Aṣṭalakṣmī (8 Lakṣmīs). Consort of Śiva (Pārvatī), Viṣṇu (Lakṣmī), Brahmā (Sarasvatī). Festivals: Navarātrī/Durgā Pūjā, Vasanta Navarātrī, Kālī Pūjā, Lakṣmī Pūjā, Sarasvatī Pūjā. Śākta Pīṭhas: 51/108 sites (Kāmākhyā, Kālikā, Jvālāmukhī, Viśālākṣī). --- The Goddess in her manifold forms; this record represents the broad category of Devī-centered traditions without collapsing their distinct textual and ritual expressions.

deity.title: Gaṇeśa
deity.description: Gaṇeśa (गणेश / விநாயகர் / గణేష్ / ಗಣೇಶ / ഗണപതി / গণেশ / ગણેશ), Vināyaka, Piḷḷaiyār, Vighneśvara, Gajānanā — the elephant-headed deity, remover of obstacles (Vighnahartā), lord of beginnings. Son of Śiva and Pārvatī. Consorts: Siddhi (success), Buddhi (wisdom); or Ṛddhi/Siddhi. Vehicle: Mūṣaka (mouse). Attributes: broken tusk (ekadanta), modaka (sweet), axe, noose. Key texts: Gaṇeśa Purāṇa, Mudgala Purāṇa, Gaṇeśa Atharvaśīrṣa. Worshipped first in all rituals. Festivals: Gaṇeśa Caturthī (Bhādrapada Śukla Caturthī), Vināyaka Caturthī, Saṅkaṣṭī Caturthī (monthly). Regional: Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja, Pune's Dagdusheth, Tamil Nadu's Piḷḷaiyārpatti, Kerala's Koṭṭārakkara. --- A widely revered deity whose iconography, narratives, and ritual roles vary across regions, texts, and devotional communities.

deity.description: Śiva (शिव / சிவன் / ಶಿವ / ശിവന്‍ / শিব / શિવ), the Auspicious One, Maheśvara, Rudra, Paśupati, Nīlakaṇṭha, Naṭarāja (cosmic dancer), Dakṣiṇāmūrti (guru), Ardhanārīśvara (half-female). Central to Śaiva traditions (Śaiva Siddhānta, Kashmir Śaivism, Vīraśaivism, Liṅgāyat). The liṅga (aniconic form) is the primary worship focus. Twelve Jyotirliṅgas. Consort: Pārvatī/Śakti. Sons: Gaṇeśa, Skanda. Vāhana: Nandi (bull). Abode: Kailāsa. Key texts: Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Śaiva Āgamas, Tirumuṟai (Tamil). Festivals: Mahāśivarātri, Pradosha, Kārttikai Tīpam. --- A major deity with diverse textual, ritual, and regional forms; this record does not impose a single theology on the many traditions that center on Śiva.

festival.title: Dīpāvalī
festival.description: Dīpāvalī (दीपावली / தீபாவளி / ദീപാവലি / दिवाळी), the Festival of Lights (dīpa-āvalī = row of lamps). Five days: Dhanteras (wealth, Dhanvantarī), Narka Caturdashī (Kṛṣṇa slays Narakāsura), Amāvasyā (main day, Lakṣmī Pūjā, Rāma's return to Ayodhyā), Govardhan Pūjā (Kṛṣṇa lifts Govardhan), Bhāi Dooj (sibling bond). Lighting dīpas (oil lamps), rangoli, fireworks, sweets, new clothes. Regional: Kālī Pūjā (Bengal, same night), Bandi Chhor Divas (Sikh, Guru Hargobind's release), Bestu Varas (Gujarati New Year), Balipratipada (Maharashtra). Jain: Mahāvīra's nirvāṇa. The universal celebration of light over darkness, knowledge over ignorance. --- A festival of lights observed across regions and communities with varied narratives, rituals, and historical associations.

festival.title: Navarātri
festival.description: Navarātri (नवरात्रि / நவராத்திரி / നവരാത്രि / নৰরাত্রি / नवरात्री), the nine nights (nava-rātri) dedicated to the Goddess in her three guṇa-forms: Durgā (tamas, days 1-3), Lakṣmī (rajas, days 4-6), Sarasvatī (sattva, days 7-9). Autumn (Śarad, Sept-Oct) and Spring (Vasanta, Mar-Apr). Regional expressions: Durgā Pūjā (Bengal, pandals, immersion), Golu/Kolu (Tamil Nadu/Kerala, doll displays), Bathukamma (Telangana, flower stacks), Garbā/Dāṇḍiyā (Gujarat, circle dances), Mysore Dasara (royal procession), Ramlila (North, Rāma enactment), Ayudha Pūjā (tools/vehicles worship, day 9). Vijayadaśamī (day 10) = Dussehra (Rāma's victory) / Vidyarambha (initiation of learning). Fasting, devī-māhātmya recitation, kanya-pūjana (girls worshipped). ---

festival.title: Oṇam
festival.description: Oṇam (ഓണം), the state festival of Kerala, celebrated for ten days in the month of Ciṅgam (Aug-Sep). Commemorates the annual visit of Mahābali (Māvēli), the benevolent asura king, who was sent to Pātāla by Vāmana (Viṣṇu's dwarf avatāra) but granted a yearly return. Key elements: Pukkalam (floral rangoli), Oṇasadhya (feast on banana leaf with 20+ dishes), Vallam-kaḷi (snake boat races), Pulikkali (tiger dance), Tiruvaṭira (women's dance). The festival unites communities across religious lines. Glorified in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham and associated with the Tṛkkākkāra Vāmana Temple. --- A Kerala festival combining harvest commemoration with the mythological narrative of Mahabali and Vamana; its practices and narratives vary across communities and are represented here with attention to regional grounding.

festival.title: Viṣu
festival.description: Viṣu (വിഷു), the Malayalam New Year (Kolla Varṣam), observed on the first day of Meḍam (mid-April) when the Sun enters Meṣa Rāśi. The central ritual is Viṣukkaṇi (വിഷുക്കണി) — the auspicious first sight arranged the night before: a kaṇikonna (golden shower) flowers, rice, coconut, fruits, gold coins, mirror, and the Bhagavad Gītā or Rāmāyaṇa placed before Kṛṣṇa's image. Elders give Kaiṇeṭṭam (money gifts) to younger members. The Sādya feast includes viṣu-kaṭṭu (banana chips), māṅgā-caru (mango curry), and pāyaśam. Fireworks and the Viṣu-veḷḷa (boat race) at Aranmula. Marks the agricultural new year in Kerala. --- The Malayalam New Year in Kerala, marking the sun's transit into Meda Rāśi; observed with the Vishukkani (auspicious first sight), money gifts (kaineettam), and feasting.

teacher.title: Annamācārya
teacher.description: Annamācārya (1408–1503), the earliest known composer of saṅkīrtana (devotional songs) in Telugu, dedicated to Veṅkaṭeśvara of Tirumala; his 32,000+ compositions (saṅkīrtanas) on copper plates recovered in the 20th century, his role in the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition, and his influence on Carnatic music are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Appayya Dīkṣita
teacher.description: Appayya Dīkṣita (1520–1593), the Advaita Vedānta scholar and Śaiva devotee, author of over 100 works including the Siddhānta-leśa-saṅgraha, Śivārkamaṇi-dīpikā, and Khaṇḍana-khaṇḍa-khādya; his synthesis of Advaita and Śaiva Siddhānta, his debate with Vijayeन्द्र Tīrtha, and his role in the Śrīvidyā tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Kabīr
teacher.description: Kabīr (c. 1440–1518), the mystic poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, synthesizing Hindu and Islamic devotional traditions; his verses (bījak, sākhīs, śabdas) emphasizing nirguṇa-bhakti (devotion to the formless), the guru, and the critique of ritual orthodoxy; his influence on the Kabīr Panth and Sikh scripture (Gurū Granth Sāhib) is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
